observations: body L1-L4: the end of the sentence begun on p. 316. «Alcabitio» and «Albatenius» are letter-spaced. «dd3,v.–dd5,v.» and «17r.–18r.» have long dashes (4.2 and 5.4 pt); the dash after «II.» measures 9.8 pt.

body L5-L15: the minus signs are printed as dashes (9.6 to 10.2 pt) and set as minus signs. The steps of L7-L15 are right: under al-Battānī's assumption (p. 315, note 3) Dc : Da = Dβ : Dα, the semidiurnal arcs being six horary times, so that Dc = hours of distance of A × horary times of B, and with Dc = bc + Db the direction bc = Dc − Db, the form of L15. The rule (β) of L5, which renders al-Battānī's words (p. 134, L24-L26 of the translation: the product is subtracted from the right ascensions between the midheaven and the following degree), is printed with the opposite sign: it gives Db − Dc, the arc bc when b lies farther from the meridian than c, while the figure of p. 315, on which the proof is made, has b between D and c. Both give the arc bc in size. «al–Battānī» (L14) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L18-L34: the place of the Tetrabiblos is III, 10 (III, 15 of the Frankfurt version), as printed; the sign of equality measures 10.0 pt. «Ptolemaeus» (L20) is letter-spaced; «Albatenii» (L19) is not. The Greek ἔγγιστα (L24) is set as printed. The dots after «qua» (L33) are five.

body L35-L43: «Ptolemaeus», «Alcabitius», «al–Battānī» (L36), «Iohannes de Saxonia» and «Alcabitii» are letter-spaced; «Albatenius» (L39) and «Albatenii» (L43) are not. «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.4 pt), and the dash before «Ut» (L39) measures 10.2 pt. A full stop, not a comma, stands after «58,v.)» (L41) before «sicut», as printed. The place cited is p. 311, note 2.
notes_left L1-L2: the last words of chapter LV are p. 134, L46 of the translation («Hoc modo hilegia, ad vitas posita, diriguntur»).

notes_right L1-L2: «ll7,v.-mm2,r.» is printed with the gathering letters ll, like the leaf mm1 cited in the body (L41); its hyphen measures 2.5 pt. The dash of «57,r.-59,r.» measures 4.2 pt, the length of the longest hyphens of the notes.
